nodes.label: Emergencies Act Invocation (2022)

nodes.label: Chrystia Freeland

nodes.label: Nijjar Assassination (June 2023)
nodes.subtitle: Indian state-sponsored assassination on Canadian soil
nodes.detail: Hardeep Singh Nijjar shot dead outside Surrey Sikh temple. RCMP arrested 3 Indian nationals. Evidence links Indian consular staff (RAW agents) to assassination.

nodes.label: Hardeep Singh Nijjar

nodes.label: Research and Analysis Wing (RAW)
nodes.subtitle: India's external intelligence agency
nodes.detail: Canada presented evidence that RAW agents operating as visa officers in Vancouver consulate supplied information for Nijjar assassination.

nodes.label: Sanjay Kumar Verma

nodes.detail: High Commissioner expelled along with 5 other diplomats after Canada provided 'irrefutable evidence' of links between Indian govt agents and assassinations.

nodes.label: Mélanie Joly
nodes.subtitle: Foreign Affairs Minister — announced diplomat expulsions
nodes.detail: Announced expulsion of 6 Indian diplomats in Oct 2024. Presented evidence of Indian government involvement in assassinations, home invasions, drive-by shootings.

nodes.label: Sukhdool Singh

nodes.detail: Second homicide linked to Indian government agents on Canadian soil. Part of broader campaign including home invasions, shootings, arson.

nodes.label: Chatham Asset Management

nodes.label: Bell Media (BCE)

nodes.detail: Subsidiary of BCE Inc. Big Three (Bell/Rogers/Telus) control 89.7% of mobile revenue. Media arm runs CTV network, CP24, BNN Bloomberg.

nodes.label: Rogers Communications

nodes.label: CBC / Radio-Canada
nodes.subtitle: Government-funded national broadcaster
nodes.detail: Publicly funded by federal government. Rated left-center bias. Receives $1.2B+ annual parliamentary appropriation. Eligible for additional QCJO tax credits.

nodes.label: Federal Media Subsidies (QCJO)
nodes.subtitle: Government payroll subsidies + tax credits for 'qualified' media
nodes.detail: Bill C-30 (2021) created labour tax credit. Independent board designates Qualified Canadian Journalism Organizations. Creates financial dependency between media and government.

nodes.label: Afghan Detainee Scandal
nodes.subtitle: Canadian Forces transferred detainees to known torture
nodes.detail: Richard Colvin testified 'likelihood is that all Afghans we handed over were tortured.' CFNIS investigated allegations. Military police complaints filed.

nodes.label: Richard Colvin
nodes.subtitle: Diplomat — blew whistle on Afghan detainee torture transfers
nodes.detail: Testified Nov 2009 that all Afghan detainees transferred by Canada were likely tortured. Standard operating procedure for Kandahar interrogators.

nodes.label: CFNIS (Canadian Forces National Investigation Service)
nodes.subtitle: Military police investigative arm
nodes.detail: Investigates all allegations of Afghan detainee mistreatment in Canadian Forces custody. Anonymous complaints filed about prisoner abuse at Kandahar Airfield (2010-2011).

nodes.label: Phoenix Pay System Scandal
nodes.subtitle: .1B+ wasted — 80% of public servants affected
nodes.detail: IBM PeopleSoft payroll launched Feb 2016. 483,130 public servants with unresolved pay issues. .57B in overpayments. $851M paid to IBM. 408,000+ backlog as of Oct 2024.

nodes.label: IBM Canada
nodes.subtitle: 51M+ for Phoenix — designed and deployed failed system
nodes.detail: Designed and deployed Phoenix using PeopleSoft. Contract jumped from initial to 85M then to 51M+. Also helped build the business case for the system it was contracted to build (conflict of interest).

nodes.label: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC)
nodes.subtitle: Runs Phoenix pay system — managed ArriveCAN procurement
nodes.detail: Federal department responsible for Phoenix and ArriveCAN procurement. Auditor General found systemic procurement failures.

nodes.label: Aga Khan Ethics Violation
nodes.subtitle: Trudeau found guilty of 4 ethics violations (2017)
nodes.detail: PM Trudeau vacationed on Aga Khan private island. Ethics commissioner found 4 violations of Conflict of Interest Act. First sitting PM found guilty of ethics violation.

nodes.label: Aga Khan / Aga Khan Foundation
nodes.subtitle: Billionaire — hosted Trudeau on private island
nodes.detail: Spiritual leader of Ismaili Muslims. Foundation received 10M+ in federal funding. Trudeau visited private island, triggering first-ever PM ethics violation.

nodes.label: Winnipeg Lab Security Breach
nodes.subtitle: Scientists shipped Ebola to Wuhan, joined China Thousand Talents
nodes.detail: Xiangguo Qiu and Keding Cheng fired from NML Jan 2021. CSIS found Qiu intentionally transferred knowledge to PRC. Shipped Ebola + Henipah viruses to Wuhan Institute of Virology. Applied to China Thousand Talents Program.

nodes.label: Xiangguo Qiu
nodes.subtitle: NML scientist — fired for transferring secrets to China
nodes.detail: Level-4 virologist at National Microbiology Lab. CSIS: intentionally shared scientific info with PRC institutions. Shipped Ebola to Wuhan. Applied to China Thousand Talents Program. Under RCMP investigation.

nodes.label: Keding Cheng
nodes.subtitle: NML biologist — fired, husband of Xiangguo Qiu
nodes.detail: Violated lab security by inviting restricted visitors unaccompanied who removed materials. Received package from China labelled kitchen utensils containing mouse protein vials.

nodes.label: National Microbiology Lab (NML)
nodes.subtitle: Canada Level-4 virology lab — Ebola, Henipah, deadly pathogens
nodes.detail: Winnipeg-based BSL-4 facility. Handles most serious and deadly human/animal diseases. Security breach allowed virus transfers to Wuhan Institute of Virology.

nodes.label: Wuhan Institute of Virology
nodes.subtitle: Chinese lab — received Ebola from Canadian NML
nodes.detail: Received shipment of Ebola and Henipah viruses from Xiangguo Qiu in early 2019, months before she was escorted from NML.

nodes.label: NSICOP Foreign Interference Report (2024)
nodes.subtitle: Parliamentarians wittingly aiding foreign states — names classified
nodes.detail: Tabled June 3, 2024. Found some MPs/senators are witting participants in foreign interference. Accepted funds, shared privileged info, influenced colleagues on behalf of foreign missions. Names remain classified.

nodes.label: David McGuinty
nodes.subtitle: NSICOP Chair — says committee hands tied on releasing names
nodes.detail: Chair of National Security and Intelligence Committee of Parliamentarians. Tabled the explosive foreign interference report but cannot divulge identities of implicated parliamentarians.

nodes.label: Project Sidewinder (1997)
nodes.subtitle: CSIS/RCMP report on Chinese infiltration — suppressed, documents destroyed
nodes.detail: Joint CSIS-RCMP 1997 study. Found Chinese intelligence + triads controlling 200+ Canadian businesses, funding Liberal and Conservative parties. CSIS leadership ordered documents destroyed. Report gutted after political interference.

nodes.label: China Thousand Talents Program
nodes.subtitle: PRC program to recruit foreign scientists — espionage vehicle
nodes.detail: Beijing program to boost national tech capabilities. US DOJ calls it vehicle for economic espionage and IP theft. Xiangguo Qiu applied while working at NML Winnipeg.

nodes.label: Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation
nodes.subtitle: $200K Beijing-linked donation — entire board resigned
nodes.detail: Zhang Bin donated $200K in 2016. CSIS intercepted conversation where Chinese diplomat told Zhang Beijing would reimburse him. Foundation board and CEO resigned. Probe could not rule out donation was part of wider influence scheme.

nodes.label: Zhang Bin
nodes.subtitle: Beijing-linked businessman — $200K donation to Trudeau Foundation
nodes.detail: CSIS intercepted 2014 conversation with Chinese consular official discussing reimbursement for donation. China Cultural Industry Association dictated tax receipt details.

nodes.label: Alexandre Trudeau
nodes.subtitle: PM brother — signed $200K pledge without board authorization
nodes.detail: Signed the $200K donation pledge from Zhang Bin without foundation board authorization. Foundation probe found this non-compliant with Income Tax Act.

nodes.label: CERB / COVID Benefits Fraud
nodes.subtitle: $14B+ in ineligible payments — $10B still outstanding
nodes.detail: CRA sent $14B to ineligible recipients. $27.4B flagged for further scrutiny. Paid $1.6B to people who quit, $6.1M to prisoners, $1.2M to dead people, $2.2M to children under 15. 600 CRA employees investigated for fraud.

nodes.label: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
nodes.subtitle: Distributed $14B+ in ineligible COVID payments
nodes.detail: Recovered $4B of $14B in ineligible payments. $10B still outstanding. 600 own employees investigated for CERB fraud. 20 terminated. CRA shied away from full review.

nodes.label: Cullen Commission (BC Money Laundering)
nodes.subtitle: $5-7B/year laundered through BC — casinos, real estate, fentanyl
nodes.detail: Final report June 2022, 1800+ pages, 101 recommendations. Found billions laundered annually through BC casinos and real estate. Vancouver Model connected BC-Vegas-Macau casinos. Chinese high rollers with fentanyl trafficking connections.

nodes.label: Vancouver Model (Money Laundering)
nodes.subtitle: Casino-real estate laundering pipeline — $1.2B/year cash
nodes.detail: Loan sharks delivered drug-trafficking $20 bills to Chinese high rollers at BC casinos. $1.2B in cash transactions over $10K in one year. Proceeds laundered into real estate. Connected to fentanyl precursor imports from China.

nodes.label: FINTRAC (Financial Transactions)
nodes.subtitle: Canada financial intelligence unit — flagged bank accounts funding fentanyl
nodes.detail: Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada. Records suggest Chinese bank accounts funded fentanyl-precursor imports. Flagged suspicious casino transactions but enforcement lagged.

nodes.label: Conflict of Interest & Ethics Commissioner
nodes.subtitle: Found PM violated ethics laws 3x — no meaningful penalties
nodes.detail: Mario Dion found Trudeau violated Conflict of Interest Act re: Aga Khan (2017) and SNC-Lavalin (2019). Found Morneau violated 3 provisions re: WE Charity. Found LeBlanc violated re: Surf Clam contract. Max penalty: $500 fine.

nodes.label: Dominic LeBlanc
nodes.subtitle: Minister — ethics violation for $24M Surf Clam contract to cousin
nodes.detail: Found guilty of violating Conflict of Interest Act for awarding $24M Surf Clam fishing licence to company run by wife first cousin. No penalties attached. Later promoted to other cabinet portfolios.

nodes.label: Surf Clam Licence Scandal
nodes.subtitle: $24M fishing licence to minister wife cousin
nodes.detail: LeBlanc awarded lucrative Surf Clam fishing contract worth nearly $24M to company meant to be run by his wife first cousin. Ethics Commissioner found violation but no penalties.

nodes.label: Canada Infrastructure Bank (CIB)
nodes.subtitle: $35B authorized — $19B shortfall, 7 projects completed, committee recommended abolition
nodes.detail: Parliament authorized $35B over 11 years. PBO: on track to disburse only $16B ($19B shortfall). Only 7 projects completed. Not subject to normal govt transparency rules. AG has limited oversight. House transport committee recommended abolition (May 2022).

nodes.label: Mark Carney (CIB Advisory)
nodes.subtitle: Former BoC/BoE Governor — CIB advisory council ties
nodes.detail: Former Governor of Bank of Canada and Bank of England. Connected to CIB through advisory roles and Liberal economic policy. Now PM of Canada (2025).

nodes.label: National Shipbuilding Strategy
nodes.subtitle: $77B+ and rising — decades behind schedule
nodes.detail: Originally budgeted lower, now projected at $77B+. AG found costs escalating with no accountability. Canadian Surface Combatant program (15 ships) massively over budget. Irving Shipbuilding and Seaspan primary contractors.

nodes.label: C-7 Vote: 180-149 (March 11, 2021)
nodes.subtitle: 180 YEA vs 149 NAY — Liberal+Bloc passed expanded MAID
nodes.detail: Bill C-7 passed House 180-149 on March 11, 2021. Supported by most Liberals + Bloc. Opposed by Conservatives, NDP, 2 of 3 Greens. Bill Blair (Public Safety Minister controlling RCMP) voted YEA — simultaneously overseeing police AND voting to expand death legislation.

nodes.label: Anita Anand
nodes.subtitle: Defence Minister (2021-2023) — voted YEA on C-7
nodes.detail: Voted YEA on C-7. As Defence Minister oversaw National Shipbuilding Strategy cost escalation. Previously Minister of Public Services and Procurement (PSPC) during ArriveCAN period.

nodes.label: Roxham Road Crisis
nodes.subtitle: 113,000 irregular crossings — RCMP stood down, $60M+ cost
nodes.detail: 113,000 people crossed at Roxham Road 2017-2023 exploiting STCA loophole. RCMP processed but did not prevent crossings. 39,540 interceptions in 2022 alone (108/day). Facilities cost $60M+. Olympic Stadium used as housing. Closed March 25, 2023 after updated agreement.

nodes.label: Sean Fraser
nodes.subtitle: Immigration Minister (2021-2023) — presided over Roxham crisis
nodes.detail: Minister of Immigration during peak Roxham Road crossings. Oversaw updated Safe Third Country Agreement. Later became Housing Minister while housing crisis escalated.

nodes.label: Marc Miller
nodes.subtitle: Immigration Minister (2023-2025)
nodes.detail: Succeeded Sean Fraser as Immigration Minister. Presided over record immigration levels (500K+ permanent residents/year) while housing crisis deepened.

nodes.label: Opioid Crisis / Safe Supply
nodes.subtitle: 52,000+ dead since 2016 — 20 deaths/day — govt ended safe supply funding
nodes.detail: 52,000+ opioid overdose deaths since 2016. 20 deaths per day in 2024. 75% involve fentanyl. Leading cause of death for males 20-49. Health Canada ignored expert advice to expand safe supply access. Federal funding quietly ended March 2024.

nodes.label: Health Canada (Opioid Response)
nodes.subtitle: Ignored own experts, ended safe supply funding
nodes.detail: Government experts advised expanding safe drug access. Health Canada watered down support and ended safe supply funding in March 2024 while 20 Canadians died per day from overdoses.

nodes.label: Housing Affordability Crisis
nodes.subtitle: Avg price $724K — 5.1 new residents per housing start (2023)
nodes.detail: Record 1.23M population growth in 2023 (immigration). 5.1 new residents per housing unit started — highest ever. Average home $724K. Rent $2,109/month. CMHC says need to DOUBLE construction rate. No data on institutional investor ownership.

nodes.label: CMHC (Canada Mortgage and Housing)
nodes.subtitle: Crown corporation — says need 5.8M new homes by 2030
nodes.detail: Estimates 430-480K units/year needed to restore 2019 affordability. Current pace: ~245K/year. Need to double construction. No data on institutional investor footprint in housing.

nodes.label: Carbon Tax / Federal Fuel Charge
nodes.subtitle: $13B/year collected — PBO: most families net loss after rebates
nodes.detail: Federal fuel charge at $80/tonne in 2024-25. Collects $13B/year from backstop provinces. PBO: most households see net loss when fiscal AND economic impacts counted. Average family pays up to $710 more than rebate. Plus $0.4B GST collected on top of carbon tax (tax on a tax).

nodes.label: Steven Guilbeault
nodes.subtitle: Environment Minister — architect of carbon tax escalation
nodes.detail: Minister of Environment and Climate Change. Drove carbon tax increase schedule. Former Greenpeace activist. Oversaw environmental policy while Jasper burned.

nodes.label: Jasper Wildfire (July 2024)
nodes.subtitle: 358 structures destroyed, $880M insurance, 1 firefighter killed
nodes.detail: Fires merged and swept through town July 22-24, 2024. 25,000 evacuated. 358 of 1,113 structures destroyed. $880M in insurance claims. Federal-provincial jurisdictional overlap disrupted response. Parks Canada criticized for not clearing dead trees.

nodes.label: Parks Canada
nodes.subtitle: $133M federal funding for Jasper response — criticized for fire prevention failure
nodes.detail: Federal agency managing Jasper National Park. Criticized for not clearing dead trees (fuel). $133.1M federal investment for wildfire response and recovery. Jurisdictional overlap with Alberta added complexity.

nodes.label: Veterans Offered MAID Instead of Care
nodes.subtitle: Paralympian offered death instead of wheelchair ramp
nodes.detail: Christine Gauthier, Paralympic champion, testified that VAC caseworker offered her assisted dying IN WRITING after she spent 5 years trying to get a wheelchair ramp. VAC reviewed 400,000 files, found 4 cases of the same employee recommending MAID to struggling veterans instead of providing care.

nodes.label: Christine Gauthier
nodes.subtitle: Paralympian veteran — offered death instead of a wheelchair ramp
nodes.detail: Retired Cpl, Paralympic champion, Invictus Games participant. After 5 years fighting for wheelchair ramp installation, VAC caseworker offered her MAID and the equipment to do it. Testified before House of Commons committee.

nodes.label: Veterans Affairs Canada (VAC)
nodes.subtitle: Offered MAID to 4+ veterans seeking help — 40,000+ benefits backlog
nodes.detail: Caseworker offered MAID to at least 4 veterans seeking care. 400,000 files reviewed. 40,000+ veterans with pending benefits claims. VAC says MAID is not a VAC service but employee offered it anyway, in writing.

nodes.label: F-35 Fighter Jet Procurement
nodes.subtitle: 88 jets — cost jumped 46% to $27.7B, delayed to 2031
nodes.detail: 88 F-35s to replace CF-18s. Cost estimate $19B in 2022, jumped to $27.7B by 2024 (46% increase). AG found skyrocketing costs, pilot shortage, no infrastructure. Bases delayed from 2028 to 2031. No advanced jet trainer identified.

nodes.label: Vice-Admiral Mark Norman Case
nodes.subtitle: Charged for leaking shipbuilding deal — PMO accused of directing prosecution
nodes.detail: Vice-Admiral charged with breach of trust for leaking $668M shipbuilding deal. Defence alleged PMO and PCO orchestrated prosecution. Treasury Board president Scott Brison allegedly killed deal for rival Irving Shipbuilding. Charges dropped — no reasonable prospect of conviction. Norman received apology and legal fee reimbursement.

nodes.label: Vice-Admiral Mark Norman
nodes.subtitle: Charged, exonerated — PMO accused of political prosecution
nodes.detail: Second-highest ranking officer in Canadian Forces. Charged March 2018, charges dropped May 2019. Defence proved PMO interference. Received House of Commons apology, settlement, full legal fee reimbursement.

nodes.label: Scott Brison
nodes.subtitle: Treasury Board President — allegedly killed shipbuilding deal for Irving
nodes.detail: Defence alleged Brison tried to kill Davie Shipyard lease deal on behalf of rival Irving Shipbuilding in his home province of Nova Scotia. Resigned from cabinet January 2019 during Norman trial.

nodes.label: MMIWG Inquiry (Missing & Murdered Indigenous Women)
nodes.subtitle: 231 calls for justice — 5 years later, minimal to no progress
nodes.detail: Final report June 2019: concluded MMIWG crisis amounts to genocide. 231 calls for justice. 5 years later: report card found minimal to no progress on majority of calls. $2B committed but short-term funding with no impact measurement. AG found significant mismanagement of policing programs.

nodes.label: Trans Mountain Pipeline
nodes.subtitle: $34.2B (was $7.4B) — taxpayer loss $9-19B — nationalized pipeline
nodes.detail: Government bought pipeline for $4.5B in 2018. Expansion cost ballooned from $7.4B to $34.2B. Went into service May 2024. PBO: worth $29.6-33.4B = taxpayer loss. Among largest oil subsidies in the world while collecting $13B/yr carbon tax.

nodes.label: CRTC / Telecom Oligopoly
nodes.subtitle: Canadian wireless 3x UK prices — Big Three control 87% market
nodes.detail: Bell/Rogers/Telus control 86.9% of wireless subscribers and 90% of revenue. Canadian ARPU $67.41 vs UK $28.31 (2.4x). Every new entrant was acquired by Big Three. Rogers $26B Shaw acquisition further concentrated market. CRTC now requiring wholesale access.

nodes.label: Telus
nodes.subtitle: Big Three telecom — acquired Public Mobile, controls 1/3 wireless
nodes.detail: Third member of Big Three oligopoly. Acquired Public Mobile (2013). Controls roughly 1/3 of Canadian wireless market. ARPU 2.4x higher than UK equivalents.

nodes.label: Bread Price-Fixing Scandal
nodes.subtitle: 14-year conspiracy — Loblaws/Weston $500M settlement, Canada Bread $50M fine
nodes.detail: Secret agreement among bread producers and retailers to inflate prices from 2001-2015. Loblaw and George Weston paid $500M settlement. Canada Bread fined $50M (highest price-fixing fine in Canadian history). Weston received immunity for cooperating.

nodes.label: Galen Weston Jr.
nodes.subtitle: Loblaw/Weston chair — apologized for 14-year bread price-fixing
nodes.detail: Chair and CEO of George Weston Ltd. and chair of Loblaw. Companies admitted to industry-wide price-fixing arrangement. Received immunity for cooperating. Net worth estimated at $8B+. Apologized: "This behaviour should never have happened."

nodes.label: Loblaw Companies Ltd.
nodes.subtitle: Canada largest grocer — $500M bread price-fixing settlement
nodes.detail: Largest food retailer in Canada. Admitted to 14-year bread price-fixing with competitors. Paid $252.5M share of $500M settlement. Record grocery profits during inflation while Canadians used food banks at record rates.

nodes.label: Competition Bureau of Canada
nodes.subtitle: Investigated bread price-fixing — granted Loblaw immunity
nodes.detail: Investigated 14-year bread price-fixing conspiracy. Granted Loblaw/Weston immunity in exchange for cooperation. Secured $50M fine against Canada Bread (highest ever). Critics say Bureau lacks teeth for grocery pricing.

nodes.label: NATO 2% Spending Failure
nodes.subtitle: 1.37% GDP — 16,000 personnel short — target 2032, 8 years late
nodes.detail: Canada spending 1.37% GDP on defence (2024-25) vs 2% NATO commitment. PBO: will peak at 1.49% then fall. Short 16,000 personnel (8,200 regular + 7,800 reserves). 25% discount on equipment forecasts due to high likelihood of delays. Target 2032 — 18 years after pledge.

nodes.label: NDP-Liberal Supply Agreement
nodes.subtitle: NDP propped up Liberals in exchange for dental/pharmacare promises
nodes.detail: March 2022 supply and confidence agreement. NDP agreed to vote with Liberals on all crucial issues until June 2025. In exchange: dental care + pharmacare. Dental launched May 2024 (3.4M approved). Pharmacare legislation delayed repeatedly. NDP eventually tore up deal.

nodes.label: Jagmeet Singh
nodes.subtitle: NDP Leader — propped up Liberals for 2.5 years, then tore up deal
nodes.detail: Signed supply and confidence agreement keeping Trudeau in power March 2022 - September 2024. NDP voted with Liberals on all confidence matters including controversial legislation. Tore up deal September 2024 citing Liberal failure to deliver pharmacare.

nodes.label: Service Canada Collapse (Passports/EI)
nodes.subtitle: People camped outside offices — 68-day average wait for passports
nodes.detail: 2022-2023: Canadians camped outside Service Canada offices. 68-day average for passports. 80% experienced frustration. 33% made multiple trips. Workforce nearly doubled (1,365 to 2,291) to clear backlog. Passport backlog reached millions while Phoenix still broken.

nodes.label: Temporary Foreign Worker Program Abuse
nodes.subtitle: UN: breeding ground for modern slavery — Tim Hortons lobbied for higher cap
nodes.detail: United Nations dubbed Canada TFW program a breeding ground for modern slavery. Tim Hortons lobbied for 18+ months to raise worker cap from 20% to 30%. Government reduced cap to 10% in 2024. Uptick in businesses using TFWs despite high local unemployment.

nodes.label: Tim Hortons (TFW Lobbying)
nodes.subtitle: Lobbied 18+ months to raise temporary foreign worker cap
nodes.detail: Pushed federal govt to raise TFW cap from 20% to 30%. Lobbied MPs and officials in writing and in meetings for 18+ months. Government reduced cap to 10% instead.

nodes.label: NSIRA Intelligence Watchdog Budget Cuts
nodes.subtitle: Spy watchdog budget cut 15% while foreign interference explodes
nodes.detail: National Security and Intelligence Review Agency budget cut 15% as Liberals expand spy powers. NSIRA says fewer reviews possible. Called out CSIS for mischaracterizing tech use, CRA bias in terrorism audits, CSE Charter violations with polygraphs. Completed review of PRC political interference dissemination.

nodes.label: Canada-Saudi $15B Arms Deal (LAVs)
nodes.subtitle: $15B LAVs to Saudi Arabia — used in Yemen (233,000 dead)
nodes.detail: General Dynamics Land Systems Canada produced LAVs in London, Ont. Liberals approved deal originally brokered under Harper. Canadian LAVs and sniper rifles appeared in Yemen. UN: 233,000 Yemen deaths. Govt found "no credible evidence" of human rights link — Amnesty + Ploughshares called this false. $1B+ shipped in 2024 alone.

nodes.label: General Dynamics Land Systems Canada
nodes.subtitle: London ON — manufactured LAVs for Saudi $15B deal
nodes.detail: Manufactured light armoured vehicles shipped to Saudi Arabia. LAVs fitted with machine guns and cannons appeared in Yemen conflict. Deal worth $15B, largest arms export in Canadian history.

nodes.label: MindGeek / Pornhub CSAM Scandal
nodes.subtitle: 100+ survivors, 70+ MPs demanded criminal investigation — RCMP declined
nodes.detail: Montreal-based MindGeek (Pornhub parent). 100+ survivors and NGOs demanded criminal investigation. 70+ MPs from all parties called for full criminal probe. RCMP said most of 120 CSAM reports did not meet Criminal Code definition. Settlement discussions began Nov 2024.

nodes.label: First Nations Drinking Water Crisis
nodes.subtitle: 37 communities still without clean water — 30-year advisory in Neskantaga
nodes.detail: Trudeau pledged to end all 105 boil water advisories by 2021. As of 2026: 37 communities STILL under advisory. Neskantaga: 30+ years without clean water (since 1995). $6B invested, 151 advisories lifted. But nearly 50% remaining have been in place over a decade.

nodes.label: Ontario Greenbelt Scandal
nodes.subtitle: Developers gained $8.3B in land value — RCMP criminal investigation
nodes.detail: Ontario Premier Doug Ford swapped 7,400 acres out of protected Greenbelt. Developers with PC ties were main beneficiaries — $8.3B land value increase. Housing Minister + Public Services Minister both resigned. Ford apologized and reversed. RCMP launched criminal investigation.

nodes.label: Doug Ford
nodes.subtitle: Ontario Premier — Greenbelt scandal, RCMP criminal investigation
nodes.detail: Swapped protected Greenbelt land for developer allies. Auditor General: developers gained $8.3B. Two ministers resigned. Ford apologized and reversed decision. RCMP criminal investigation launched.

nodes.label: Panama/Pandora Papers (Canadian Exposure)
nodes.subtitle: Hundreds of Canadian offshore accounts — CRA identified $76M owed, collected unknown
nodes.detail: Panama Papers (2016) + Pandora Papers (2021): hundreds of Canadian offshore companies exposed. CRA identified $76M in taxes owed but cannot say if any collected. Compliance action still "in progress" years later. 29,000 offshore accounts, 336 politicians named globally.

nodes.label: Big Five Banks Record Profits
nodes.subtitle: RBC $5.1B quarterly profit while 1/3 of new mortgages unaffordable
nodes.detail: Big Five (RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank, CIBC) earned $5B+ in extra interest income since rates rose. RBC: $5.13B quarterly profit (Q1 2025). Savings rates stuck below 2% while lending rates soared. Over 1/3 of new mortgages exceed 25% debt service ratio (double 2019). Growing spread between lending and savings rates drives record profits.

nodes.label: COVID School Closures (Longest in Canada: Ontario)
nodes.subtitle: 64% youth mental health damaged — 2x suicide admissions, 3x substance use
nodes.detail: Ontario had longest school closures in Canada (2020-2022). 64% of youth 15-24 reported negative mental health impact. Children hospitals: 2x suicide attempt admissions, 3x substance use admissions, 60% increase in eating disorders. Math and reading scores dropped. Lifelong costs imposed on a generation.

nodes.label: Lytton BC Rebuild Failure
nodes.subtitle: Town destroyed 2021 — only 17 of 45 homes rebuilt 4 years later
nodes.detail: Wildfire destroyed Lytton June 30, 2021. 2 dead, 250+ displaced. $239M+ in recovery funding. 4 years later: only 17/45 homes rebuilt. No town hall, hospital, bank, or food mart. 60% had no fire insurance. AG: province was unprepared, village "immediately overwhelmed."

nodes.label: Diploma Mill / International Student Fraud
nodes.subtitle: 10,000+ fake acceptance letters — students exploited and trafficked
nodes.detail: IRCC uncovered 10,000+ fraudulent student acceptance letters in 2024. 80% linked to Gujarat and Punjab students. 260+ Canadian colleges linked to illegal US border crossings. Fake agents, fictitious universities, stolen credit cards. 1,485 students deported. UN: TFW program is modern slavery.

nodes.label: Food Bank Crisis (2M+ visits/month)
nodes.subtitle: 2 million food bank visits/month — 90% increase since 2019, 700K children
nodes.detail: March 2024: 2,059,636 food bank visits — record. Up 90% from 2019. 1/3 of clients are children (700K/month). 18% are employed (working poor). 30% of food banks running out of food. Driven by housing costs, inflation, insufficient social supports.

nodes.label: Auto Theft / Organized Crime Export
nodes.subtitle: 2,277 stolen vehicles intercepted — less than 1% of containers scanned
nodes.detail: CBSA intercepted 2,277 stolen vehicles in 2024. Montreal port: saturated with organized criminals shipping stolen cars to Africa/Middle East. Less than 1% of containers scanned. Only 8 border officers at port. Cars packed into containers at warehouses. 17% decline after national action plan.

nodes.label: Asylum Seeker Hotel Housing ($1.1B+)
nodes.subtitle: $1.1B+ on hotels for asylum seekers — 46 hotels, $208/person/day
nodes.detail: 5,000 asylum seekers housed in Montreal hotels (Feb 2023-Feb 2024). Average 113 days at $208/person/day. IRCC rented rooms in 46 hotels. Total bill $115M in one city alone. Quebec received $750M federal funding for asylum costs. Roxham Road costs: $1.5B+ total to taxpayers.

nodes.label: Bell Media: 4,800 Layoffs While Taking Subsidies
nodes.subtitle: 4,800+ jobs cut, 45 radio stations sold — after $122M in govt subsidies
nodes.detail: BCE cut 4,800+ jobs in Feb 2024, sold 45 radio stations. Total 6,000+ fired. Received $122M from Emergency Wage Subsidy. Worth $40B. Hiked executive pay and shareholder payouts with one hand while firing workers with the other. Heritage Minister called it "extremely disappointing."

nodes.label: Forced Labour Imports (Bill S-211 Failure)
nodes.subtitle: Only 1 shipment blocked vs US blocking billions — Uyghur forced labour goods entering Canada
nodes.detail: Bill S-211 took effect Jan 2024. CBSA has only blocked 1 shipment vs US blocking billions in goods. No meaningful enforcement guidance issued. US scrutinizing Canada failure. Chinese solar modules detained worth $5M+ face lawsuit. Reporting obligations but no teeth.

nodes.label: Federal Debt: $1.28 Trillion
nodes.subtitle: $1.28T debt — $54B/year interest — projected $82B/year by 2031
nodes.detail: Federal debt $1,266.5B at March 2025. Interest payments $53.8B in 2024-25. PBO projects interest to reach $82.4B/year by 2030-31. Debt projected to rise to $1.655T by 2030-31. Debt service consuming 10.8% of all federal revenues and rising.

nodes.label: Healthcare Crisis (6M without family doctor)
nodes.subtitle: 6M Canadians no family doctor — 500K left ER unseen — 1 in 5 Ontario ERs closed
nodes.detail: 6 million Canadians without family physician. Deficit of 22,823 family doctors. 500K left ERs without seeing a doctor in 2024. 2024 worst year for Ontario ER closures (38 hospitals). 92% of doctors in cities, 8% in rural areas. 1,300 new graduates/year vs 22K shortage.
